name: Kohath
summary: Second son of Levi, who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household. He was the grandfather of Moses, Aaron and Miriam, and his descendants, the Kohathites, were charged with carrying the most holy things of the tabernacle, including the ark.
catholic: Kohath matters chiefly as the link in the priestly genealogy from Levi to Aaron. The Kohathite duty of bearing the ark and the holy vessels (Num 4) shows that in Israel holiness required ordered, appointed ministry, a theme the Church sees fulfilled in the ordered ministries of the New Covenant.
know: Son of Levi; went down to Egypt with Jacob (Gen 46:11).
Father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
Kohathites carried the ark and holy furnishings but could not touch or look on them (Num 4:15-20).

name: Gershon
summary: Eldest son of Levi. His descendants, the Gershonites, carried the curtains and coverings of the tabernacle in the wilderness.
know: Gershonites carried the tabernacle's curtains and hangings (Num 4:24-28).

name: Merari
summary: Third son of Levi. His descendants, the Merarites, carried the boards, bars, pillars and sockets of the tabernacle.

name: Libni
summary: Son of Gershon and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

name: Shimei
summary: Son of Gershon and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

name: Mahli
summary: Son of Merari and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

name: Mushi
summary: Son of Merari and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

name: Amram
summary: Son of Kohath and grandson of Levi. He married his aunt Jochebed, and they became the parents of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.
catholic: Amram is honoured in Scripture chiefly through his children. Hebrews 11:23 praises the faith of Moses' parents, who hid the child and 'were not afraid of the king's commandment' - an example the Church holds up of parents protecting the life of a child against an unjust decree.
know: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi.
Father of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.

name: Jochebed
summary: Levite woman, daughter of Levi and wife of Amram, mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam. When Pharaoh ordered Hebrew boys drowned, she hid the infant Moses for three months, then set him in a papyrus basket on the Nile - and was hired by Pharaoh's daughter to nurse her own son.
catholic: Jochebed is a model of courageous motherhood defending a child's life against a death-decree, a scene the Fathers compared with the Holy Family's flight from Herod. The ark-basket (the same Hebrew word as Noah's ark) in which she placed Moses has been read as a figure of salvation through water, and her faith is praised in Hebrews 11:23.
know: Daughter of Levi; wife of Amram (Num 26:59).
Hid Moses three months and placed him in a basket on the Nile (Exo 2:2-3).
Was paid to nurse her own son (Exo 2:9).
Mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.

name: Moses
summary: Levite born in Egypt under Pharaoh's death-decree, drawn from the Nile and raised by Pharaoh's daughter. After killing an Egyptian he fled to Midian, married Zipporah, and was called by God from the burning bush, where the divine name was revealed. He led Israel out of Egypt through the Red Sea, received the Law at Sinai, interceded for the people after the golden calf, and led them forty years in the wilderness; he died on Mount Nebo in sight of the promised land.
catholic: The Church sees Moses as the great type of Christ: the deliverer spared from a king's massacre, the mediator of the covenant, and the prophet who foretold 'a prophet like me' (Deut 18:15; Acts 3:22). The Law came through Moses, grace and truth through Jesus Christ (Jn 1:17); Moses gave manna, but the Father gives the true bread from heaven (Jn 6:32), and the bronze serpent he lifted up prefigures the Cross (Jn 3:14). The Catechism presents the burning bush and the revelation of the divine name (CCC 205-209) and Moses as the model of intercessory prayer (CCC 2574-2577). He appears with Elijah at the Transfiguration, and the Roman Martyrology commemorates him on September 4.
know: Name explained as 'drawn out of the water' (Exo 2:10).
Received God's name 'I AM WHO I AM' at the burning bush (Exo 3:14).
Led the Exodus and received the Ten Commandments at Sinai.
Called the most humble man on earth, speaking with God 'mouth to mouth' (Num 12:3-8).
Died on Mount Nebo; 'no prophet has arisen in Israel like Moses' (Deut 34:10).

name: Aaron
summary: Elder brother of Moses, appointed by God as his spokesman before Pharaoh. He was anointed the first high priest of Israel, and his sons were made priests in perpetuity. He made the golden calf at the people's demand, joined Miriam in murmuring against Moses, and his rod alone budded when the tribes' rods were tested; he died on Mount Hor and his vestments passed to Eleazar.
catholic: The Church sees in Aaron's priesthood a prefiguration of the priesthood of the New Covenant. The Catechism teaches that the liturgy recognizes in the priesthood of Aaron and the service of the Levites a prefiguring of the ordained ministry, which is fulfilled in Christ, the one high priest (CCC 1539-1541; Heb 5:1-10). Hebrews contrasts Christ, a priest 'after the order of Melchizedek', with the Aaronic priests. Aaron's priestly blessing (Num 6:22-27) is the first reading on January 1, the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God, and his rod that blossomed without root has been read in tradition as a figure of the Virgin's fruitfulness. The Roman Martyrology commemorates him on July 1.
know: His rod budded, blossomed and bore almonds (Num 17:8).

name: Miriam
summary: Sister of Moses and Aaron, called a prophetess. She led the women in song and dance after the crossing of the Red Sea. When she and Aaron spoke against Moses she was struck with leprosy and shut out of the camp seven days; she died at Kadesh.
catholic: Miriam's song at the sea (Exo 15:20-21) is one of the oldest hymns of Scripture, and the Canticle of Moses is sung at Lauds and proclaimed at the Easter Vigil. Christian writers have long noted that Mary, the Mother of Jesus, bears Miriam's name, and have compared Miriam's song of deliverance with Mary's Magnificat. Micah 6:4 counts her with Moses and Aaron among those God sent before Israel.
know: Usually identified with the sister who watched over the infant Moses (Exo 2:4-8).
Struck with leprosy after criticizing Moses (Num 12).

name: Zipporah
summary: Daughter of Jethro (Reuel), priest of Midian, given to Moses as wife after he defended her and her sisters at a well. She bore him Gershom and Eliezer and, on the road back to Egypt, circumcised her son to avert the LORD's threat against Moses.
catholic: Zipporah's urgent circumcision of her son (Exo 4:24-26) underlines the seriousness of the covenant sign, which the Church sees fulfilled in Baptism, the 'circumcision of Christ' (Col 2:11-12). As a Midianite woman joined to Moses she is also read as a sign of the nations being drawn into God's people.
know: Daughter of the priest of Midian (Exo 2:16-21).
Circumcised her son with a flint (Exo 4:25).
Brought back to Moses by Jethro at Sinai (Exo 18:2-6).
Whether the 'Cushite woman' of Num 12:1 is Zipporah or a second wife is debated.

name: Jethro
summary: Priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses, also called Reuel. He sheltered Moses for forty years, gave him his daughter Zipporah, and later came to Sinai, praised the LORD for the deliverance from Egypt, offered sacrifice, and advised Moses to appoint judges to share the burden of governing the people.
catholic: Jethro is a Gentile who blesses the God of Israel and offers sacrifice (Exo 18:10-12), and so is read as a figure of the nations coming to faith. His counsel that Moses delegate authority to capable men (Exo 18:13-26) has been cited by Church writers as a model of shared, ordered governance.
know: Father of Zipporah and of Hobab.
Confessed 'Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods' (Exo 18:11).
Advised Moses to appoint judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.

name: Hobab
summary: Son of Reuel the Midianite and brother-in-law of Moses. Moses urged him to journey with Israel and serve as their 'eyes' in the wilderness; his descendants, the Kenites, later settled among Judah.
know: Moses asked him to guide Israel through the wilderness (Num 10:31).
Ancestor of the Kenites, including Heber, husband of Jael.

name: Gershom
summary: Firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian; Moses named him Gershom, saying, 'I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land.' Judges 18:30 names his son Jonathan as priest to the Danites' idol.
know: Ancestor of Jonathan, the Danites' priest (Jdg 18:30), and of Shebuel (1 Chr 23:16).

name: Eliezer
summary: Second son of Moses and Zipporah. Moses named him Eliezer ('my God is help'), saying that the God of his father had delivered him from Pharaoh's sword.

name: Pharaoh's daughter
summary: Daughter of the Pharaoh who ordered the Hebrew boys drowned. She found the infant Moses in a basket among the reeds, had compassion on him, hired his own mother as nurse, and raised him as her son, giving him his name.
catholic: Pharaoh's daughter shows mercy that defies her father's death-decree, and God uses a Gentile woman's compassion to preserve Israel's deliverer. Stephen recalls her in his speech (Acts 7:21), and Hebrews 11:24 notes that Moses by faith refused to be called her son.
know: Named him Moses, 'because I drew him out of the water' (Exo 2:10).

name: Pharaoh of the Oppression
summary: The 'new king who did not know Joseph', who enslaved the Israelites, ordered the midwives to kill Hebrew boys, and then commanded that every newborn son be thrown into the Nile. Moses fled from him to Midian; he died while Israel still groaned in slavery.
catholic: The Fathers set this Pharaoh's slaughter of the Hebrew infants beside Herod's massacre of the Innocents (Mt 2:16), seeing in Moses' rescue a figure of the Christ Child's escape.
know: 'A new king arose over Egypt, who didn't know Joseph' (Exo 1:8).
His death is noted in Exo 2:23; Scripture does not name him.

name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
summary: The king of Egypt whom Moses and Aaron confronted with the LORD's command, 'Let my people go.' He hardened his heart through ten plagues, released Israel only after the death of the firstborn, then pursued them and lost his army in the Red Sea.
catholic: Pharaoh is Scripture's great image of the heart that hardens itself against God; St. Paul cites him in Romans 9:17 on God's sovereignty in salvation history. The deliverance from his power through the sea is, for the Church, the type of Baptism (CCC 1221), and the Easter Vigil's reading of Exodus 14 celebrates Christ's victory over sin and death as the true Exodus.
know: Answered Moses, 'Who is the LORD, that I should listen to his voice?' (Exo 5:2).
Ten plagues culminated in the death of the firstborn (Exo 12:29-32).
His chariots were drowned in the Red Sea (Exo 14:23-28).

name: Shiphrah
summary: One of two Hebrew midwives ordered by Pharaoh to kill newborn Hebrew boys. Fearing God, she and Puah let the boys live, and God dealt well with them and gave them households.
catholic: Shiphrah and Puah are often cited in Catholic teaching as early examples of conscientious refusal to take innocent life at the command of the state: they 'feared God' rather than the king (Exo 1:17).
know: Refused Pharaoh's order to kill the boys.
God rewarded her with a household (Exo 1:21).

name: Puah
summary: The second of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill the Hebrew baby boys.
catholic: With Shiphrah, Puah is held up as a witness to the dignity of human life and to obeying God rather than an unjust law.
know: Defied Pharaoh to save newborn boys.
Not the same as Puah, father of the judge Tola.

name: Elisheba
summary: Daughter of Amminadab of Judah and sister of Nahshon, prince of Judah. She married Aaron and bore Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, so that the priestly line of Israel descends from her.
catholic: Elisheba unites the priestly tribe of Levi with the royal tribe of Judah. Some Christian writers note that her name is the Hebrew form of 'Elizabeth', borne by the priestly mother of John the Baptist, who was 'of the daughters of Aaron' (Lk 1:5).
know: Daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahshon (Exo 6:23).
Mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

name: Nadab
summary: Eldest son of Aaron. With Abihu and the seventy elders he saw the God of Israel on Sinai, but after his ordination he and Abihu offered 'strange fire' before the LORD, and fire came out and consumed them.
catholic: The death of Nadab and Abihu is read as a sober lesson that worship must be offered as God commands, not according to human invention - a theme the Church applies to reverence in the liturgy.
know: Saw God on Sinai with the elders (Exo 24:9-11).

name: Abihu
summary: Second son of Aaron. He ascended Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Nadab and the seventy elders, but was struck down with Nadab for offering strange fire.
catholic: As with Nadab, his fate is read as a warning against irreverent or self-willed worship.
know: Saw the God of Israel on Sinai (Exo 24:9-10).

name: Eleazar
summary: Third son of Aaron, who succeeded his father as high priest when Moses transferred Aaron's vestments to him on Mount Hor. He took the census on the plains of Moab, commissioned Joshua with Moses, and with Joshua divided the land among the tribes; he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim.
catholic: Eleazar embodies the continuity of the priesthood through succession: the office passes from Aaron to his son by a visible rite of investiture. The Church sees in this an Old Testament witness to an ordered, handed-on priesthood, fulfilled in Christ and continued in the ministerial priesthood.
know: Joshua was to stand before him and inquire by the Urim (Num 27:21).

name: Ithamar
summary: Youngest son of Aaron. He oversaw the accounting of the tabernacle materials and supervised the Gershonite and Merarite Levites in the wilderness. The priestly house of Ithamar continued alongside that of Eleazar.
know: Later priestly courses were divided between Eleazar's and Ithamar's houses (1 Chr 24:3-4).

name: Phinehas
summary: Son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron. When an Israelite brought a Midianite woman into the camp during the apostasy at Peor, Phinehas killed them both, the plague stopped, and God gave him 'a covenant of an everlasting priesthood'. He later led the delegation to the tribes east of the Jordan and served as priest at Bethel in the days of the judges.
catholic: Phinehas is Scripture's emblem of zeal for God's honour: Psalm 106:30-31 says it was 'credited to him for righteousness', and Sirach 45:23-24 calls him 'third in glory' after Moses and Aaron. Mattathias explicitly modelled his zeal on Phinehas (1 Mac 2:26, 54). The covenant of perpetual priesthood granted to him (Num 25:13) is read by the Church as finding its fulfilment in the eternal priesthood of Christ.
know: Son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron (Exo 6:25).
Received 'the covenant of an everlasting priesthood' (Num 25:13).
Ministered before the ark in Judges 20:28.

name: Izhar
summary: Son of Kohath and brother of Amram; father of Korah, who led the rebellion against Moses and Aaron.
know: Father of Korah, Nepheg and Zichri (Exo 6:21).

name: Hebron
summary: Son of Kohath and brother of Amram; ancestor of the Hebronite clan of Levites.
know: Not to be confused with the city of Hebron.

name: Uzziel
summary: Son of Kohath and uncle of Aaron; his sons Mishael and Elzaphan carried the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp.
know: Son of Kohath, uncle of Moses and Aaron (Lev 10:4).
Father of Mishael, Elzaphan and Sithri.

name: Mishael
summary: Son of Uzziel and cousin of Aaron. At Moses' command he and Elzaphan carried their kinsmen Nadab and Abihu out of the camp after the LORD's fire consumed them.
know: Carried Nadab and Abihu's bodies from the sanctuary (Lev 10:4-5).

name: Elzaphan
summary: Son of Uzziel, cousin of Aaron. He helped carry out the bodies of Nadab and Abihu, and as Elizaphan was made prince of the Kohathite clans.
know: Called Elizaphan, prince of the Kohathites (Num 3:30).
Helped remove Nadab and Abihu's bodies (Lev 10:4).

name: Korah
summary: Levite, son of Izhar and cousin of Moses and Aaron. With Dathan, Abiram, On and 250 leaders he challenged the authority of Moses and the priesthood of Aaron, claiming that all the congregation was holy. The earth swallowed the rebels' households and fire consumed the 250 who offered incense, but Korah's sons did not die.
catholic: Korah's rebellion is the classic biblical case of rejecting divinely instituted authority and grasping at priesthood not given by God; Jude 11 names it among the sins of false teachers, and Sirach 45:18-19 recalls it. The Church has read it as a warning against schism and against claiming sacred office without a call. His surviving descendants became temple singers, and many Psalms are titled 'of the sons of Korah'.
know: Son of Izhar, grandson of Kohath (Exo 6:21).
Led a revolt against Moses and Aaron (Num 16).
Cited in Jude 11 ('the rebellion of Korah').

name: Assir
summary: Assir was a son of Korah listed in the Levitical genealogy of Exodus 6; the line of Korah survived the rebellion and later supplied temple singers.
know: Korah's sons did not die in the rebellion (Num 26:11).

name: Elkanah
summary: Elkanah was a son of Korah listed in the Levitical genealogy of Exodus 6; the line of Korah survived the rebellion and later supplied temple singers.
know: Korah's sons did not die in the rebellion (Num 26:11).

name: Abiasaph
summary: Abiasaph was a son of Korah listed in the Levitical genealogy of Exodus 6; the line of Korah survived the rebellion and later supplied temple singers.
know: Korah's sons did not die in the rebellion (Num 26:11).

name: Hur
summary: Leader of Israel who, with Aaron, went up the hill with Moses during the battle against Amalek and held up Moses' hands until sunset, so Israel prevailed. When Moses ascended Sinai he left Aaron and Hur in charge of the people.
catholic: The image of Aaron and Hur supporting the arms of Moses at prayer (Exo 17:12) has been used by the Fathers as a figure of the outstretched arms of Christ on the Cross, and more widely of the support the faithful give to the prayer of their shepherds.
know: Held up Moses' hands with Aaron at Rephidim (Exo 17:10-12).
Left in charge with Aaron while Moses was on Sinai (Exo 24:14).
Jewish tradition identifies him with the grandfather of Bezalel, but Scripture does not say so.

name: Hur (grandfather of Bezalel)
summary: Man of Judah, grandfather of the craftsman Bezalel through his son Uri. 1 Chronicles makes him a son of Caleb son of Hezron and Ephrath.
know: Father of Uri and grandfather of Bezalel (Exo 31:2).
Possibly the same as Moses' companion Hur; Scripture does not say.

name: Uri
summary: Son of Hur of the tribe of Judah and father of Bezalel, the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
know: Son of Hur, father of Bezalel (Exo 31:2).

name: Bezalel
summary: Son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, whom God called by name and filled with the Spirit of God in wisdom and skill. He led the work of making the tabernacle, the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat, the lampstand and the priestly vessels.
catholic: Bezalel is the first person in Scripture said to be 'filled with the Spirit of God' (Exo 31:3), and his gift is artistic: the Church sees in him a patron-figure for sacred art and architecture placed at the service of worship. The ark he made, overshadowed by the cherubim, is in Catholic tradition a type of Mary, the Ark of the New Covenant.
know: Called by name and filled with God's Spirit (Exo 31:1-5).
Made the ark of the covenant (Exo 37:1-9).
Worked with Oholiab and other skilled workers.
His bronze altar still stood at Gibeon in Solomon's day (2 Chr 1:5).

name: Oholiab
summary: Son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, appointed by God to assist Bezalel. He was an engraver, designer and embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet, and teacher of others in the work of the tabernacle.
catholic: With Bezalel, Oholiab shows that craftsmanship and beauty serve the worship of God; the pairing of a man of Judah and a man of Dan has been noted as all Israel contributing to the sanctuary.

name: Ahisamach
summary: Danite, father of the craftsman Oholiab.

name: Shelomith
summary: Daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan, whose son by an Egyptian father blasphemed the Name in a quarrel in the camp and was stoned at the LORD's command.
know: Mother of the blasphemer of Lev 24.

name: Dibri
summary: Man of the tribe of Dan, father of Shelomith.

name: Son of Shelomith (the blasphemer)
summary: Son of an Israelite mother, Shelomith, and an Egyptian father, who cursed the Name of the LORD during a fight in the camp. He was held until the LORD's will was known, then stoned outside the camp, and the law against blasphemy was given.
catholic: The episode underlies the Second Commandment's teaching on reverence for God's name, which the Catechism treats under the commandment 'You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain' (CCC 2142).
know: Unnamed; son of Shelomith and an Egyptian (Lev 24:10).
Occasion of the law in Lev 24:15-16.

name: Elizur
summary: Son of Shedeur and leader of the tribe of Reuben in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Reuben's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Shedeur, prince of Reuben (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Reuben's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:30).

name: Shelumiel
summary: Son of Zurishaddai and leader of the tribe of Simeon in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Simeon's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Zurishaddai, prince of Simeon (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Simeon's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:36).

name: Nethanel
summary: Son of Zuar and leader of the tribe of Issachar in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Issachar's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Zuar, prince of Issachar (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Issachar's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:18).

name: Eliab
summary: Son of Helon and leader of the tribe of Zebulun in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Zebulun's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Helon, prince of Zebulun (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Zebulun's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:24).

name: Elishama
summary: Son of Ammihud and leader of the tribe of Ephraim in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Ephraim's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar. According to 1 Chronicles 7:26-27 he was the grandfather of Joshua.
know: Son of Ammihud, prince of Ephraim (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Ephraim's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:48).
1 Chronicles 7:26-27 lists Elishama son of Ammihud as father of Nun and grandfather of Joshua.

name: Gamaliel
summary: Son of Pedahzur and leader of the tribe of Manasseh in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Manasseh's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Pedahzur, prince of Manasseh (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Manasseh's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:54).

name: Abidan
summary: Son of Gideoni and leader of the tribe of Benjamin in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Benjamin's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Gideoni, prince of Benjamin (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Benjamin's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:60).

name: Ahiezer
summary: Son of Ammishaddai and leader of the tribe of Dan in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Dan's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Ammishaddai, prince of Dan (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Dan's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:66).

name: Pagiel
summary: Son of Ochran and leader of the tribe of Asher in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Asher's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Ochran, prince of Asher (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Asher's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:72).

name: Eliasaph
summary: Son of Deuel and leader of the tribe of Gad in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Gad's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Deuel, prince of Gad (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Gad's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:42).

name: Ahira
summary: Son of Enan and leader of the tribe of Naphtali in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Naphtali's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Enan, prince of Naphtali (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Naphtali's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:78).

name: Eldad
summary: One of the seventy elders chosen to share Moses' burden. Though he stayed in the camp rather than going to the Tent of Meeting, the Spirit rested on him and he prophesied; when Joshua asked Moses to stop him, Moses replied, 'I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets.'
catholic: The episode (read on the 26th Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year B, with Mk 9:38-48) is used to teach that the Spirit is not confined by human boundaries, and Moses' wish that all God's people be prophets is seen as fulfilled at Pentecost (Acts 2:17-18) and in the prophetic office shared by all the baptized.
know: Prophesied in the camp with Medad.

name: Medad
summary: Elder of Israel who, with Eldad, received the Spirit and prophesied in the camp, prompting Moses' wish that all the LORD's people were prophets.
catholic: See Eldad: their story is read as an image of the Spirit's freedom and the prophetic dignity of all God's people.
know: Prophesied in the camp with Eldad (Num 11:26-27).
Joshua's jealousy for Moses was gently rebuked.

name: Shammua
summary: Son of Zaccur, the man of Reuben among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Reuben among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Shaphat
summary: Son of Hori, the man of Simeon among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Simeon among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Igal
summary: Son of Joseph, the man of Issachar among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Issachar among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Palti
summary: Son of Raphu, the man of Benjamin among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Benjamin among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Gaddiel
summary: Son of Sodi, the man of Zebulun among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Zebulun among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Gaddi
summary: Son of Susi, the man of Manasseh among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Manasseh among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Ammiel
summary: Son of Gemalli, the man of Dan among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Dan among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Sethur
summary: Son of Michael, the man of Asher among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Asher among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Nahbi
summary: Son of Vophsi, the man of Naphtali among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Naphtali among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Geuel
summary: Son of Machi, the man of Gad among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Gad among the twelve spies (Num 13).

name: Pallu
summary: Son of Reuben who went down to Egypt with Jacob; ancestor of the Palluite clan and grandfather of Dathan and Abiram.

name: Eliab
summary: Reubenite, son of Pallu, and father of Dathan, Abiram and Nemuel.
know: Son of Pallu, grandson of Reuben (Num 26:8).

name: Dathan
summary: Reubenite, son of Eliab, who with his brother Abiram joined Korah's rebellion. Refusing Moses' summons, they accused him of bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to die in the wilderness; the earth opened and swallowed them with their households.
catholic: Dathan and Abiram are remembered in the Psalms and Sirach as an example of rebellion against God's chosen leaders and of the judgement that follows (Ps 106:16-18; Sir 45:18).
know: Refused to come up at Moses' call (Num 16:12-14).

name: Abiram
summary: Reubenite, son of Eliab and brother of Dathan, who joined Korah's revolt against Moses and Aaron and was swallowed by the earth with his household.
catholic: Like Dathan, he stands in Scripture as a warning against contempt for God-given authority (Ps 106:17).
know: Son of Eliab, brother of Dathan.

name: On
summary: Reubenite, son of Peleth, named at the start of Korah's rebellion with Dathan and Abiram, though he is not mentioned again.
know: Named among Korah's allies but not in the judgement scene.

name: Beor
summary: Father of the diviner Balaam.

name: Balaam
summary: Diviner from Pethor by the Euphrates, son of Beor, hired by King Balak of Moab to curse Israel. God stopped him through a talking donkey and an angel, and instead of cursing he blessed Israel four times, prophesying 'a star will come out of Jacob, a scepter will rise out of Israel.' He later counselled Moab and Midian to lead Israel into sin at Peor and was killed with the kings of Midian.
catholic: Balaam's oracle of the star out of Jacob (Num 24:17) was read by Origen and other Fathers as fulfilled in the star that led the Magi to Christ. The New Testament treats Balaam as a type of the false teacher who sells his gift for gain (2 Pet 2:15; Jude 11; Rev 2:14), a warning the Church applies to anyone who traffics in sacred things.
know: Hired by Balak to curse Israel (Num 22:5-6).
His donkey saw the angel and spoke (Num 22:22-35).
Prophesied 'a star will come out of Jacob' (Num 24:17).
Counselled the sin at Peor; killed among the Midianites (Num 31:8, 16).

name: Zippor
summary: Father of Balak, king of Moab.

name: Balak
summary: Son of Zippor and king of Moab, who, afraid of Israel camped on the plains of Moab, summoned Balaam to curse them. He led Balaam to three high places, but each time Balaam blessed Israel instead.
catholic: Balak illustrates that no human power can curse those whom God has blessed; Micah 6:5 calls Israel to remember what Balak plotted and what Balaam answered, as part of recalling the 'righteous acts of the LORD'. Revelation 2:14 recalls how Balaam taught Balak to cast a stumbling block before Israel.
know: Son of Zippor, king of Moab (Num 22:4).
Remembered in Jos 24:9, Jdg 11:25, Mic 6:5 and Rev 2:14.

name: Salu
summary: Simeonite, father of Zimri.

name: Zimri
summary: Son of Salu and a prince of the tribe of Simeon, who during the apostasy at Baal Peor brought the Midianite woman Cozbi into his tent in the sight of Moses and the congregation; Phinehas killed them both and the plague stopped.
know: Son of Salu, a leader of Simeon (Num 25:14).

name: Cozbi
summary: Daughter of Zur, a Midianite chief, killed by Phinehas together with Zimri during the apostasy at Peor.
know: Daughter of Zur, head of a Midianite house (Num 25:15).

name: Evi
summary: One of the five kings (princes) of Midian killed by Israel in the war of vengeance for Peor, in which Balaam was also slain; Joshua 13:21 calls them princes of Sihon.
know: One of the five kings of Midian (Num 31:8).
Killed in Israel's war against Midian.

name: Rekem
summary: One of the five kings (princes) of Midian killed by Israel in the war of vengeance for Peor, in which Balaam was also slain; Joshua 13:21 calls them princes of Sihon.
know: One of the five kings of Midian (Num 31:8).
Killed in Israel's war against Midian.

name: Zur
summary: One of the five kings (princes) of Midian killed by Israel in the war of vengeance for Peor, in which Balaam was also slain; Joshua 13:21 calls them princes of Sihon. His daughter Cozbi was killed with Zimri at Peor.
know: One of the five kings of Midian (Num 31:8).
Killed in Israel's war against Midian.

name: Hur
summary: One of the five kings (princes) of Midian killed by Israel in the war of vengeance for Peor, in which Balaam was also slain; Joshua 13:21 calls them princes of Sihon.
know: One of the five kings of Midian (Num 31:8).
Killed in Israel's war against Midian.

name: Reba
summary: One of the five kings (princes) of Midian killed by Israel in the war of vengeance for Peor, in which Balaam was also slain; Joshua 13:21 calls them princes of Sihon.
know: One of the five kings of Midian (Num 31:8).
Killed in Israel's war against Midian.

name: Sihon
summary: Amorite king ruling from Heshbon who refused Israel passage through his land and attacked them; Israel defeated him and took his territory east of the Jordan, which Moses gave to Reuben and Gad.
catholic: The victories over Sihon and Og became part of Israel's liturgical memory of God's saving deeds, celebrated in Psalms 135 and 136 ('for his loving kindness endures forever').
know: King of the Amorites at Heshbon (Num 21:26).
Refused Israel passage and was defeated (Num 21:21-25).

name: Og
summary: King of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, whose iron bedstead was nine cubits long. He came out against Israel at Edrei and was defeated, and his kingdom was given to the half-tribe of Manasseh.
catholic: With Sihon, Og is named in Psalms 135 and 136 among the kings God struck down for his people.
know: Last of the Rephaim; his bed was nine cubits long (Deut 3:11).

name: Machir
summary: Firstborn son of Manasseh, born in Egypt and raised on Joseph's knees. His descendants, the Machirites, conquered Gilead east of the Jordan, which Moses gave them.
know: Son of Manasseh; his children were born on Joseph's knees (Gen 50:23).

name: Gilead
summary: Son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh, ancestor of the Gileadite clans including Hepher.

name: Hepher
summary: Son of Gilead of Manasseh, father of Zelophehad.
know: Son of Gilead, father of Zelophehad (Num 26:32-33).

name: Zelophehad
summary: Son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh, who died in the wilderness without sons. His five daughters asked for his inheritance, leading to the law that daughters inherit when there is no son.
know: Died in the wilderness, not in Korah's rebellion (Num 27:3).
Had five daughters and no sons.
His case set Israel's inheritance law (Num 27:8-11).

name: Mahlah
summary: Mahlah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).

name: Noah
summary: Noah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).

name: Hoglah
summary: Hoglah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).

name: Milcah
summary: Milcah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).

name: Tirzah
summary: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).

name: Jair (son of Manasseh)
summary: Descendant of Manasseh who captured the villages of Gilead and Argob and named them Havvoth Jair, 'the villages of Jair'.
know: Called 'son of Manasseh' (Num 32:41), i.e. a descendant.
Took villages east of the Jordan and named them Havvoth Jair.
Not the judge Jair of Judges 10.

name: Nun
summary: Man of the tribe of Ephraim, father of Joshua. 1 Chronicles 7 places him in the line of Ephraim as son of Elishama son of Ammihud.

name: Joshua
role: Leader of Israel, successor of Moses
summary: Son of Nun of Ephraim, originally named Hoshea; Moses renamed him Joshua. He was Moses' assistant, fought Amalek at Rephidim, stayed at the Tent of Meeting, and with Caleb gave the faithful report about Canaan. Commissioned as Moses' successor, he led Israel across the Jordan, took Jericho and much of the land, divided it among the tribes, and before his death renewed the covenant at Shechem: 'As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.'
catholic: Joshua bears the same name as Jesus (Hebrew Yehoshua, 'the LORD saves'; Greek Iesous), and the Fathers, beginning with St. Justin Martyr, saw in him a vivid type of Christ: not Moses the lawgiver but Joshua/Jesus leads God's people into the promised rest (Heb 4:8). The crossing of the Jordan is presented by the Catechism, with the crossing of the Red Sea, as a figure of Baptism (CCC 1222). His renewal of the covenant at Shechem (Jos 24) is a model of personal and household fidelity. The Roman Martyrology commemorates him on September 1.
know: One of only two adults of the Exodus generation to enter Canaan (Num 14:30).
Led the crossing of the Jordan and the fall of Jericho (Jos 3-6).
Commanded the sun to stand still at Gibeon (Jos 10:12-14).
'As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD' (Jos 24:15).

name: Jephunneh
summary: The Kenizzite father of Caleb.

name: Caleb
summary: Son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, the spy from Judah who, with Joshua, urged Israel to trust God and take the land. God promised that because he 'followed me fully' he would enter Canaan. At eighty-five he claimed Hebron, drove out the three sons of Anak, and gave his daughter Achsah to Othniel for capturing Kiriath Sepher.
catholic: Caleb is the Bible's portrait of wholehearted fidelity and undiminished strength in old age (Jos 14:10-11); Sirach 46:7-10 praises him with Joshua, and 1 Maccabees 2:56 says he received an inheritance 'for testifying in the congregation'. The Church holds him up as an example of courageous witness against the discouragement of the crowd.
know: 'Let's go up at once, and possess it' (Num 13:30).
Had 'another spirit' and followed God fully (Num 14:24).

name: Kenaz
summary: Father of the judge Othniel. Joshua 15:17 and Judges 1:13 call Othniel 'son of Kenaz, Caleb's (younger) brother'.
know: Related to Caleb; whether Kenaz or Othniel is meant as Caleb's brother is debated.

name: Othniel
summary: Son of Kenaz, of Caleb's family, who captured Kiriath Sepher (Debir) and won Caleb's daughter Achsah as wife. When Israel served Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia for eight years, the Spirit of the LORD came upon him; he delivered Israel and the land had rest forty years. He is the first of the judges.
catholic: Othniel is the model judge in whom the pattern of the book is laid out plainly: sin, oppression, crying out, a Spirit-filled deliverer, and rest. The Church reads the judges' Spirit-given deliverance as a foreshadowing of Christ, on whom the Spirit rests fully (Isa 11:2; Lk 4:18).
know: Took Kiriath Sepher and married Achsah (Jos 15:17).
The land had rest forty years (Jdg 3:11).

name: Achsah
summary: Daughter of Caleb, promised to whoever captured Kiriath Sepher and given to Othniel. She urged her husband to ask for a field and herself asked her father for springs of water, receiving the upper and lower springs.
catholic: Achsah's bold, successful petition to her father has been used by spiritual writers as an image of confident prayer to God the Father.
know: Asked for and received springs of water (Jos 15:18-19).

name: Rahab
summary: Canaanite woman of Jericho, called a prostitute, who hid Joshua's two spies, confessed that 'the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above and on earth beneath', and let them down by a rope from her house on the wall. A scarlet cord in her window marked her household, which was spared when Jericho fell; she lived among Israel and, according to Matthew, married Salmon and became the mother of Boaz.
catholic: Rahab is one of the four women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:5), a sign that the Messiah came for Gentiles and sinners. Hebrews 11:31 praises her faith and James 2:25 her works, so she is a classic witness that faith and works go together. St. Clement of Rome (1 Clement 12) saw in the scarlet cord a sign of redemption through the blood of the Lord, and the Fathers read her house, the only place of safety in the doomed city, as a figure of the Church.
know: Hid the spies and confessed faith in the LORD (Jos 2:9-11).
Spared with her family at Jericho (Jos 6:22-25).

name: Zabdi
summary: Judahite of the clan of Zerah, grandfather of Achan.
know: Son of Zerah, father of Carmi (Jos 7:1).

name: Carmi
summary: Judahite, son of Zabdi and father of Achan.
know: Not Carmi the son of Reuben.

name: Achan
summary: Judahite, son of Carmi, who at the fall of Jericho secretly took a mantle, silver and a wedge of gold that had been devoted to the LORD. Israel was then defeated at Ai; Achan was identified by lot, confessed, and was stoned with his household in the Valley of Achor.
catholic: Achan's hidden sin bringing defeat on all Israel is a scriptural image of the communal dimension of sin, which the Catechism describes: every sin harms the communion of the Church. His confession before Joshua ('give glory to the LORD... and make confession') is often cited in teaching on the confession of sins.
know: His sin caused the defeat at Ai.
Stoned in the Valley of Achor (Jos 7:24-26).
Called Achar, 'the troubler of Israel' (1 Chr 2:7).

name: Adoni-Zedek
summary: Amorite king of Jerusalem who, alarmed at Gibeon's treaty with Israel, formed a coalition of five kings to attack Gibeon. Joshua routed them in the battle when the sun stood still; the kings hid in a cave at Makkedah and were executed.
catholic: His name ('my lord is righteousness') echoes that of Melchizedek, earlier king of Salem; Christian writers have contrasted the unjust king of Jerusalem with Christ, the true King of Righteousness.
know: Led the five-king coalition against Gibeon.

name: Hoham
summary: King of Hebron, one of the five Amorite kings who joined Adoni-Zedek against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua and executed at Makkedah.

name: Piram
summary: King of Jarmuth, one of the five Amorite kings who joined Adoni-Zedek against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua and executed at Makkedah.

name: Japhia
summary: King of Lachish, one of the five Amorite kings who joined Adoni-Zedek against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua and executed at Makkedah.

name: Debir
summary: King of Eglon, one of the five Amorite kings who joined Adoni-Zedek against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua and executed at Makkedah.

name: Jabin (in Joshua)
summary: King of Hazor who gathered the kings of northern Canaan against Israel at the waters of Merom. Joshua defeated the coalition, killed Jabin and burned Hazor.
know: King of Hazor, head of the northern kingdoms (Jos 11:10).
Defeated at the waters of Merom (Jos 11:7-8).
A later Jabin of Hazor oppressed Israel in Deborah's day (Jdg 4:2).

name: Jobab
summary: King of Madon summoned by Jabin of Hazor to join the northern coalition against Joshua.

name: Arba
summary: Great man among the Anakim, father of Anak, after whom Kiriath Arba (Hebron) was named.

name: Anak
summary: Ancestor of the Anakim, the giant clan of Hebron whose size terrified the ten spies.
know: The spies felt 'like grasshoppers' beside his descendants (Num 13:33).
Father of Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai.

name: Ahiman
summary: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron when the spies came; Caleb (and Judah) later drove them out.

name: Sheshai
summary: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron when the spies came; Caleb (and Judah) later drove them out.

name: Talmai
summary: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron when the spies came; Caleb (and Judah) later drove them out.

name: Adoni-Bezek
summary: Canaanite king defeated by Judah and Simeon at Bezek. His captors cut off his thumbs and big toes, and he confessed that God had repaid him for doing the same to seventy kings.

name: Cushan Rishathaim
summary: King of Mesopotamia (Aram-naharaim) to whom the LORD gave Israel for eight years until Othniel delivered them.

name: Gera
summary: Benjamite, father of the judge Ehud.

name: Ehud
summary: Left-handed Benjamite, son of Gera, raised up by the LORD when Israel had served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years. Bringing tribute, he gained a private audience, killed the obese king with a hidden double-edged sword, escaped, and led Israel to victory; the land had rest eighty years.
catholic: Ehud's 'secret message from God' (Jdg 3:20) has been read allegorically by the Fathers of the two-edged word of God (Heb 4:12) that pierces to the heart. More broadly he shows God choosing the unlikely - a left-handed man of the smallest tribe - to save his people.
know: Killed Eglon of Moab with a hidden sword (Jdg 3:21-22).
Rallied Israel at the fords of the Jordan.

name: Eglon
summary: King of Moab who, allied with Ammon and Amalek, took Jericho (the city of palms) and ruled Israel eighteen years, until Ehud assassinated him.

name: Anath
summary: Named as the parent of the judge Shamgar ('son of Anath').

name: Shamgar
summary: Son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an ox goad and also saved Israel. The Song of Deborah dates the perilous days when the highways were deserted to 'the days of Shamgar'.
know: Killed 600 Philistines with an ox goad (Jdg 3:31).
Named in the Song of Deborah (Jdg 5:6).

name: Jabin (in Judges)
summary: King of Canaan reigning in Hazor who oppressed Israel cruelly for twenty years with nine hundred iron chariots under his commander Sisera, until the victory of Deborah and Barak; Israel then pressed on until they destroyed him.

name: Sisera
summary: Commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan, with nine hundred chariots of iron. Routed by Barak at the Kishon, he fled on foot to the tent of Heber the Kenite, where Jael gave him milk and then drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept.
catholic: Sisera's fall at the hand of a woman is celebrated in the Song of Deborah; the Fathers saw in it how God brings down the proud through the lowly, a theme echoed in Mary's Magnificat (Lk 1:52).
know: Killed by Jael with a tent peg (Jdg 4:21).
His mother waits at the window in the Song of Deborah (Jdg 5:28).

name: Lappidoth
summary: Husband of the prophetess and judge Deborah.
know: Deborah is called 'the wife of Lappidoth' (Jdg 4:4).

name: Deborah
summary: Prophetess, wife of Lappidoth, who judged Israel under the palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel. She summoned Barak to fight Sisera, went with him into battle, and foretold that the LORD would deliver Sisera into the hand of a woman. With Barak she sang the victory song of Judges 5, and the land had rest forty years.
catholic: Deborah, 'a mother in Israel' (Jdg 5:7), is honoured as one of the great women of the Old Testament - a prophetess who speaks God's word and calls others to courageous action. Christian tradition has seen in the valiant women of Israel, such as Deborah, Jael and Judith, foreshadowings of Mary, whose fiat and victory over the enemy are celebrated in the Church's liturgy.
know: Judged under 'the palm tree of Deborah'.

name: Abinoam
summary: Man of Kedesh in Naphtali, father of Barak.

name: Barak
summary: Son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, called by Deborah to lead ten thousand men against Sisera. He would go only if Deborah went with him, and so the honour of killing Sisera went to a woman; he routed Sisera's chariots at the Kishon and sang with Deborah.
catholic: Hebrews 11:32 lists Barak among the heroes of faith 'who through faith subdued kingdoms'. His dependence on the prophetic word spoken through Deborah is read as an example of obedience to God's voice in the community.
know: Named among the faithful in Heb 11:32.

name: Heber the Kenite
summary: Kenite descended from Hobab, Moses' brother-in-law, who had separated from his clan and camped near Kedesh; he was at peace with Jabin. Sisera fled to the tent of his wife Jael.
know: At peace with Jabin of Hazor (Jdg 4:17).

name: Jael
summary: Wife of Heber the Kenite, who welcomed the fleeing Sisera into her tent, gave him milk, covered him, and while he slept drove a tent peg through his temple, fulfilling Deborah's word that the LORD would sell Sisera into a woman's hand.
catholic: The Song of Deborah calls Jael 'blessed above women' (Jdg 5:24), words echoed of Judith (Jdt 13:18) and of Mary by Elizabeth (Lk 1:42). Patristic and medieval writers read her, like Judith, as a type of Mary, through whom the enemy's head is crushed (cf. Gen 3:15).
know: Killed Sisera with a tent peg (Jdg 4:21).

name: Joash the Abiezrite
summary: Man of Ophrah of the clan of Abiezer in Manasseh, father of Gideon. When the townsmen demanded Gideon's death for destroying Baal's altar, Joash replied, 'If he is a god, let him contend for himself.'
know: Owned the altar of Baal Gideon tore down.

name: Gideon
summary: Son of Joash of the clan of Abiezer in Manasseh, called by the angel of the LORD while threshing wheat in a winepress during the Midianite oppression. He tore down his father's altar of Baal (earning the name Jerubbaal), sought signs with a fleece, and with only three hundred men bearing trumpets and torches in jars routed the Midianite host. He refused kingship, but his gold ephod became a snare to Israel.
catholic: The Fathers, notably St. Ambrose, read the fleece wet with dew while the ground stayed dry as a figure of the Virgin Mary, who received the Word as dew from heaven; the Liturgy of the Hours for January 1 sings that Christ came down 'like rain upon the fleece'. Gideon's small band shows that victory comes from God, not from human strength. Hebrews 11:32 names him among the heroes of faith, and the Roman Martyrology commemorates him on September 1.
know: Called while threshing in a winepress (Jdg 6:11-12).
Named Jerubbaal after destroying Baal's altar (Jdg 6:32).
Asked for the sign of the fleece (Jdg 6:36-40).
Refused to be king: 'the LORD shall rule over you' (Jdg 8:23).

name: Purah
summary: Gideon's servant, who went down with him at night to the Midianite camp, where they overheard a soldier's dream of a barley loaf overturning a tent.
know: Overheard the dream of the barley loaf with Gideon.

name: Oreb
summary: One of the two princes of Midian during Gideon's war, captured and killed by the Ephraimites at the rock of Oreb; his head was brought to Gideon.
know: Remembered in Ps 83:11 among God's defeated enemies.

name: Zeeb
summary: One of the two princes of Midian during Gideon's war, captured and killed by the Ephraimites at the winepress of Zeeb; his head was brought to Gideon.
know: Remembered in Ps 83:11 among God's defeated enemies.

name: Zebah
summary: One of the two kings of Midian pursued by Gideon across the Jordan. Captured at Karkor, they admitted killing Gideon's brothers at Tabor, and Gideon killed them himself.

name: Zalmunna
summary: One of the two kings of Midian pursued by Gideon across the Jordan. Captured at Karkor, they admitted killing Gideon's brothers at Tabor, and Gideon killed them himself.

name: Jether
summary: Gideon's firstborn, who as a youth was told to kill the captured kings Zebah and Zalmunna but was afraid to draw his sword.
know: Too afraid to kill the Midianite kings.

name: Gideon's concubine in Shechem
summary: Gideon's concubine from Shechem, mother of Abimelech, through whose kin in Shechem Abimelech seized power.

name: Abimelech (son of Gideon)
summary: Son of Gideon by his concubine in Shechem. With money from the temple of Baal Berith he hired men, murdered his seventy brothers on one stone, and was made king at Shechem. After three years God sent an evil spirit between him and Shechem; he destroyed the city, but at Thebez a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head and he had his armour-bearer kill him.
catholic: Abimelech is Scripture's portrait of the usurper who grasps at kingship by violence, the bramble of Jotham's fable; his end illustrates that God repays bloodshed (Jdg 9:56-57). He stands in contrast to the servant-kingship of Christ.
know: Mortally wounded by a millstone thrown by a woman (Jdg 9:53; 2 Sam 11:21).

name: Jotham (son of Gideon)
summary: Youngest son of Gideon, the only one to escape Abimelech's massacre. From Mount Gerizim he told the people of Shechem the fable of the trees who sought a king and ended with the bramble, cursing Shechem and Abimelech; then he fled to Beer.
catholic: Jotham's fable (Jdg 9:7-15), the oldest fable in Scripture, is a classic critique of power seized by the unworthy; the curse he pronounced is said to have come upon both Abimelech and Shechem (Jdg 9:57).
know: Youngest son of Gideon; hid and survived (Jdg 9:5).
Told the fable of the trees from Gerizim (Jdg 9:7-15).

name: Ebed
summary: Father of Gaal, who rebelled against Abimelech.

name: Gaal
summary: Son of Ebed, who won the trust of Shechem and boasted against Abimelech; Zebul warned Abimelech, who defeated Gaal and drove him out of the city.

name: Zebul
summary: Ruler of the city of Shechem under Abimelech, who secretly warned him of Gaal's revolt, taunted Gaal, and expelled Gaal's kin from the city.

name: Dodo
summary: Man of Issachar, grandfather of the judge Tola.
know: Father of Puah, grandfather of Tola (Jdg 10:1).

name: Puah (father of Tola)
summary: Man of Issachar, son of Dodo and father of the judge Tola.

name: Tola
summary: Son of Puah son of Dodo, of Issachar, who rose to save Israel after Abimelech and judged Israel twenty-three years, living in Shamir in Ephraim.

name: Jair (judge)
summary: Gileadite who judged Israel twenty-two years; he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys and ruled thirty towns called Havvoth Jair.

name: Gilead (father of Jephthah)
summary: Gileadite father of Jephthah by a prostitute; his legitimate sons later drove Jephthah out of the family inheritance.

name: Jephthah
summary: Mighty warrior of Gilead, son of Gilead by a prostitute, driven out by his half-brothers and living as a raider in Tob. When Ammon attacked, the elders of Gilead made him their head. After arguing Israel's case to the Ammonite king, he made a rash vow to offer whatever first came out of his house if he returned victorious; he defeated Ammon, and his only daughter came out to meet him. He judged Israel six years.
catholic: Hebrews 11:32 lists Jephthah among those who through faith conquered kingdoms, yet St. Jerome (quoted by St. Thomas Aquinas) judged him 'foolish in vowing and impious in keeping' his vow, and the Church uses his story as a warning about imprudent vows; the Catechism teaches that vows must concern a 'better good' that is possible (CCC 2102). His daughter's acceptance has been compared by some writers to self-offering, but Scripture presents the vow itself as a tragedy.
know: Son of Gilead by a prostitute (Jdg 11:1).
Made head of Gilead against Ammon (Jdg 11:4-11).

name: Jephthah's daughter
summary: Jephthah's only child, who came out with timbrels and dances to meet her victorious father and became the subject of his vow. She asked for two months to mourn her virginity on the mountains with her companions; afterward her father 'did to her according to his vow', and the daughters of Israel lamented her four days each year.
catholic: Her obedience and the annual lament of Israel's daughters have moved many Christian writers; some later interpreters argued she was dedicated to perpetual virginity rather than sacrificed, though the text is commonly read as a sacrifice. Either way, the Church reads her story as a condemnation of rash vows and of any 'offering' of innocent human life.

name: Ibzan
summary: Judge from Bethlehem who judged Israel seven years; he had thirty sons and thirty daughters and arranged marriages for them all outside his clan.

name: Elon
summary: Zebulunite who judged Israel ten years and was buried at Aijalon in Zebulun.

name: Hillel
summary: Pirathonite, father of the judge Abdon.

name: Abdon
summary: Son of Hillel the Pirathonite, who judged Israel eight years; he had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys, and was buried in Pirathon in Ephraim.

name: Manoah
summary: Danite of Zorah whose barren wife was told by the angel of the LORD that she would bear a son to be a Nazirite from the womb. Manoah prayed for the angel to return, asked his name (it is 'incomprehensible'), and offered a sacrifice; the angel ascended in the altar's flame.
catholic: The annunciation of Samson's birth to a barren mother, with a heavenly messenger and a consecrated child, belongs to the pattern the Church sees culminating in the annunciations to Zechariah and to Mary (Lk 1). The angel's answer that his name is 'incomprehensible' (Jdg 13:18; the Hebrew word is related to 'wonderful') is often linked by Christian readers with the messianic title 'Wonderful Counselor' (Isa 9:6).
know: Prayed for the angel to return (Jdg 13:8).
Saw the angel ascend in the altar flame (Jdg 13:20).

name: Wife of Manoah (mother of Samson)
summary: Barren Danite woman to whom the angel of the LORD appeared, announcing that she would bear a son who would be a Nazirite to God from the womb and begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. She was to drink no wine and eat nothing unclean.
catholic: Her story stands in the line of barren mothers whose sons are gifts of God - Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Hannah, Elizabeth - and so prepares for the annunciation to Mary. Her calm faith ('if the LORD were pleased to kill us, he wouldn't have received a burnt offering', Jdg 13:23) contrasts with Manoah's fear.
know: Told to abstain from wine and unclean food (Jdg 13:4).

name: Samson
summary: Son of Manoah of Dan, a Nazirite from birth whose strength depended on his consecration. He killed a lion barehanded, married a Philistine woman of Timnah, struck down a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone, and carried off the gates of Gaza. Betrayed by Delilah, who had his hair cut, he was blinded and enslaved; in his death he pulled down the temple of Dagon, killing more Philistines than in his life. He judged Israel twenty years.
catholic: Hebrews 11:32 counts Samson among the heroes of faith. Patristic writers saw him as a type of Christ: his birth announced by an angel, his strength from the Spirit, his betrayal for silver, his outstretched arms between the pillars, and a victory won in his death. At the same time he is a warning about squandering a consecration through sensuality, and his Nazirite vow (Num 6) points to a life wholly given to God.
know: Killed a lion and posed the riddle of honey (Jdg 14).
Struck a thousand men with a jawbone (Jdg 15:15).
Betrayed by Delilah, blinded at Gaza (Jdg 16:4-21).

name: Samson's wife from Timnah
summary: Philistine woman of Timnah whom Samson married against his parents' wishes. Under threat from the Philistines she pressed Samson to reveal his riddle, then was given to his companion; in revenge for Samson's attack, the Philistines burned her and her father.

name: Delilah
summary: Woman of the valley of Sorek whom Samson loved. Bribed by the Philistine lords with eleven hundred pieces of silver each, she pressed him until he revealed that his strength lay in his uncut hair, then had it shaved while he slept and handed him to the Philistines.
catholic: Delilah's betrayal of Samson for silver has been compared by Christian writers to Judas' betrayal of Christ. Her persistent pressure is also a classic image of temptation that wears down resistance.

name: Micah's mother
summary: Ephraimite woman who cursed the thief of her 1,100 pieces of silver; when her son Micah confessed and returned it, she blessed him and had part of it made into a carved and a molten image for his shrine.
know: Cursed the theft, then blessed her son (Jdg 17:2).
Dedicated silver to make idols 'for the LORD' (Jdg 17:3-4).

name: Micah (of Ephraim)
summary: Man of the hill country of Ephraim who returned stolen silver to his mother, set up a household shrine with images, an ephod and teraphim, and hired a wandering Levite as his priest. The migrating Danites stole his images and his priest, and he could not resist them.
catholic: Micah's shrine illustrates the confusion of the period when 'there was no king in Israel; everyone did that which was right in his own eyes' (Jdg 17:6): worship invented by private initiative rather than received from God. The Church reads it as a contrast with true, ordered worship.
know: Lived in the hill country of Ephraim (Jdg 17:1).
Made a shrine with images and an ephod (Jdg 17:5).

name: Jonathan (son of Gershom)
summary: Young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah who became Micah's household priest, then went with the Danites, who set up Micah's image at Laish (Dan). Judges 18:30 identifies him as 'Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Moses', whose sons were priests to Dan until the captivity.
know: Levite from Bethlehem who served Micah (Jdg 17:7-13).
Went with the Danites as their priest (Jdg 18:19-20).
Grandson (descendant) of Moses (Jdg 18:30; the Hebrew text has a suspended letter making 'Manasseh').

name: The Levite of Judges 19
summary: Levite living in the remote hill country of Ephraim whose concubine left him for her father's house in Bethlehem. Returning with her, he lodged in Gibeah of Benjamin, where the men of the town abused her through the night until she died. He cut her body into twelve pieces and sent them through Israel, provoking war against Benjamin.
catholic: The story shows the moral collapse of an Israel without a king (Jdg 19:1; 21:25). The Church reads it as an indictment of violence against women and as preparing for God's gift of a righteous king, ultimately Christ.
know: Levite from the hill country of Ephraim (Jdg 19:1).
Sent his concubine's body through Israel (Jdg 19:29).

name: The Levite's concubine
summary: Woman of Bethlehem in Judah, concubine of the Levite of Judges 19, who was given over to the men of Gibeah, abused through the night, and found dead at the door at dawn. Her death led to the war against Benjamin.
catholic: Her story, one of the darkest in Scripture, is read as a lament over human cruelty and the failure of protectors; Hosea recalls 'the days of Gibeah' as a byword for corruption (Hos 9:9; 10:9).

name: Hezron
summary: Son of Perez and grandson of Judah, who went down to Egypt with Jacob. He heads the genealogy of Ruth 4 that leads to David, and is the ancestor of the Hezronite clan.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ.
know: Went down to Egypt with Jacob.

name: Ram
summary: Son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah and father of Amminadab, known only from the genealogies leading to David and to Jesus. Luke calls him Aram.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ.

name: Amminadab
summary: Man of Judah, son of Ram, father of Nahshon the prince of Judah and of Elisheba, wife of Aaron - so that the royal line of Judah and the priestly line of Aaron meet in his household.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ. Through his daughter Elisheba he is also grandfather of Israel's priests.
know: Father of Nahshon and of Elisheba, Aaron's wife (Exo 6:23).
In the genealogies of Mt 1:4 and Lk 3:33.

name: Nahshon
summary: Son of Amminadab and prince of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness. He helped Moses take the census, led the camp of Judah at the head of Israel's march, and was the first leader to present his tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar. He was brother-in-law of Aaron and grandfather of Boaz.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ. Jewish tradition (not Scripture) remembers him as the first to step into the Red Sea.
know: Son of Amminadab, prince of Judah (Num 1:7; 2:3).
First to bring his offering for the altar (Num 7:12).

name: Salmon
summary: Son of Nahshon of Judah and father of Boaz. Matthew's genealogy names Rahab of Jericho as the mother of Boaz, making Salmon her husband.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ. His marriage to Rahab (Mt 1:5) brings a Canaanite woman of faith into the Messiah's ancestry.

name: Elimelech
summary: Man of Bethlehem in Judah who, during a famine in the days of the judges, took his wife Naomi and sons Mahlon and Chilion to Moab, where he died. Boaz redeemed his land and raised up his name through Ruth.

name: Naomi
summary: Wife of Elimelech of Bethlehem. Widowed in Moab and bereaved of both sons, she returned home calling herself Mara ('bitter'), accompanied by her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth. She guided Ruth to Boaz, and when Obed was born the women said, 'A son is born to Naomi.'
catholic: Naomi's journey from emptiness to fullness is read as a parable of God's hidden providence. The Church's tradition has seen in the bond of Naomi and Ruth a picture of Israel welcoming the Gentiles, and Naomi nursing Obed, the grandfather of David, as the hidden preparation for the Messiah.
know: Wife of Elimelech, mother of Mahlon and Chilion (Ruth 1:2).

name: Mahlon
summary: Elder son of Elimelech and Naomi, who married Ruth in Moab and died there childless; Boaz acquired Ruth 'to raise up the name of the dead' on his inheritance.

name: Chilion
summary: Younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, who married the Moabite Orpah and died in Moab.

name: Orpah
summary: Moabite widow of Chilion who set out with Naomi but, at Naomi's urging, kissed her and returned to her people and her gods.
catholic: Orpah's departure throws Ruth's fidelity into relief; spiritual writers contrast the two as the soul that turns back and the soul that clings to God.

name: Ruth
summary: Moabite widow of Mahlon who refused to leave her mother-in-law Naomi: 'Where you go, I will go... your people will be my people, and your God my God.' Gleaning in the fields of Boaz at Bethlehem, she won his kindness, sought him as redeemer at the threshing floor, and became his wife. Their son Obed was the grandfather of King David.
catholic: Ruth is one of the four women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:5), a Gentile who by faith and loving-kindness (hesed) enters the people of God and becomes an ancestress of the Messiah - a sign of the universal reach of salvation. Her words to Naomi are a classic expression of covenant fidelity and are often used at weddings. Boaz as her kinsman-redeemer has long been read as a figure of Christ, who takes the Gentile Church as his bride.
know: 'Your people will be my people, and your God my God' (Ruth 1:16).
Great-grandmother of David; named in Mt 1:5.

name: Boaz
summary: Wealthy landowner of Bethlehem, kinsman of Elimelech, son of Salmon (and of Rahab, per Matthew). He showed kindness to the gleaner Ruth, and when she asked him to spread the corner of his garment over her as near kinsman, he settled the claim of a nearer kinsman at the town gate, bought Elimelech's land, and married Ruth. Their son Obed was David's grandfather.
catholic: The Church Fathers read Boaz, the go'el (kinsman-redeemer) who freely takes the poor foreign widow as his bride, as a figure of Christ the Redeemer who unites the Church of the Gentiles to himself. Born in Bethlehem and ancestor of David, he stands in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:5). His greeting to the reapers, 'The LORD be with you' (Ruth 2:4), echoes in the liturgy.
know: Acted as kinsman-redeemer at the city gate (Ruth 4:1-10).
Husband of Ruth, father of Obed.

name: Obed
summary: Son of Boaz and Ruth, born in Bethlehem and nursed by Naomi; the neighbour women named him. He was the father of Jesse and grandfather of King David.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ.
know: Named by the women of Bethlehem (Ruth 4:17).
Father of Jesse, grandfather of David (Ruth 4:17, 22).

name: Jesse
summary: Bethlehemite, son of Obed and grandson of Boaz and Ruth, father of eight sons, the youngest of whom, David, was anointed king by Samuel. His name stands at the close of the book of Ruth as the link to David.
catholic: Isaiah's prophecy of 'a shoot from the stock of Jesse' on whom the Spirit of the LORD will rest (Isa 11:1-2) is read by the Church as fulfilled in Christ, and Paul cites 'the root of Jesse' (Rom 15:12). From this text come the medieval 'Tree of Jesse' images and the Advent Jesse Tree, and the 'O Radix Jesse' antiphon of the O Antiphons (December 19). Tradition has also seen Mary as the 'rod' (virga) from Jesse's root.
know: A Bethlehemite with eight sons (1 Sam 16:1; 17:12).
'A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse' (Isa 11:1).
